issues.issue: "Place tremendous value in our investment banking relationships" and "significant step" are promotional expressions with no ascertainable content, so a court could be asked whether they are mere puffery or a commitment. The provision supplies no standard against which "broad based, high quality investment banking services" could be measured.

"Well suited to this situation" is an unmeasurable evaluative phrase stated as a feeling ("We feel"), leaving it uncertain whether anything is being represented at all. A court would have to decide whether this is opinion or an actionable statement of capability.

"Unparalleled auction rate performance" (along with "unique idea generation" and "a sincere desire") is a superlative with no defined benchmark, and the open-ended "These strengths include:" leaves the list's outer reach undetermined. In an auction-rate context a court would have to decide what performance, if any, was promised by that word.

"The commitment and depth of services that we are prepared to provide" is hedged by "We hope that this proposal helps to demonstrate," so it is unclear whether any service level is being undertaken. The words "commitment" and "depth" have no defined content.

This is a garbled RFP question whose bulleted service list has been interleaved with the question text, so which services are within "the following key services" cannot be read off the page. The enumeration is also introduced as "key services," leaving unclear whether the list is exhaustive of what was requested.

"A full range of investing, advisory, and financing services" is a descriptive corporate self-description whose boundary ("full range") is undefined. It is descriptive rather than promissory, so the risk of construction is modest.

"Complete, broad based, intensive coverage ... regardless of where they are in their capital cycle" uses three unquantified adjectives, and "intensive coverage" has no ascertainable content. A court asked whether a service standard was undertaken would have to construe these words.

"Focusing on what is best for the client rather than what produces the next trade" is precisely the kind of phrase a client invokes to assert a duty of loyalty, and its scope (advice only? principal transactions?) is undefined. "Product innovator and market leader" is likewise unmeasurable.

"Govern our approach to all of our business activities" leaves it uncertain whether the Business Principles appended as Appendix A are binding obligations or aspirational statements. "Govern" is the word a court would have to construe.

"Our clients' interests always come first" is the classic quoted principle a client relies on to assert a fiduciary or loyalty obligation, and the sentence gives no limits on when or how it applies. Its status as an incorporated quotation from Appendix A rather than an undertaking is itself the thing to be construed.

"Charged with accessing and directing the Firm's vast resources" states an internal duty without saying to whom it is owed or what performance it requires. "Vast resources" has no measurable boundary.

"Similar to those sought by Presbyterian" ties an enumerated list of past services to an undefined comparison, so which of the listed services are actually being offered here is left open. "Have included" also signals a non-exhaustive list of uncertain reach.

"All found that an integrated approach created the greatest level of financing success" is an unverifiable characterisation of other clients' experience, not a term with operative content. There is little here for a court to construe as an obligation.

"Leader and innovator in each of the service areas desired by Presbyterian" is a superlative claim with no benchmark, applied to a semicolon-separated list whose completeness is unstated. Whether "leader" was a representation or puffery is the question a court would face.
"Greatest value" through "integration of these areas of expertise" is an unquantified marketing conclusion referring to an external case study. It carries no term with an applicable boundary.

The provision opens with a truncated heading fragment ("FORMATION STRATEGI") and consists otherwise of the unmeasurable phrase "we take the long view of capital formation." Neither the heading nor the phrase has determinable content.

"Includes variables such as" introduces an open-ended enumeration whose outer limit is undefined, and the list itself is corrupted ("optimal cost of capitat organizational strategic initiatives") so that one item runs into the next. A reader cannot tell where one listed variable ends and another begins.

"Optimal debt and investment portfolios" and "cost/risk objectives and existing constraints" set no standard by which optimality could be judged. Whether this describes a tool or promises an outcome is left open.

"Can assist" states a capability rather than an undertaking, and the "e.g." list of debt features leaves the range of analysis offered undefined. A court would have to decide whether anything was promised to Presbyterian at all.

"Has the capability to" and "help devise strategies" describe what the model can do without committing to doing it, leaving the scope of any service undetermined. The sentence's single run-on structure also blurs which capabilities are being claimed.

The sentence breaks off mid-clause at "whose organization and finances are complex and lend", so the criterion limiting use of the tool is literally incomplete and unascertainable. "A select group of clients" is in any event an undefined boundary.

This restriction of the CSM tool to "only a select group of clients" sits uneasily with the offers made in the preceding provisions that "The model can assist Presbyterian" (c022) and evaluate Presbyterian's exposures (c023), which assume the tool is available to Presbyterian. A court would have to reconcile the limitation with those statements and with the CSM description reserving the model for "the firm's largest and most prestigious" clients.
